title: Repair request-session window correctness and throughput
statement_md:
# Request-session window report

An operations service looks for the longest consecutive stretch of requests containing
at most K distinct error codes. Two regressions were introduced: the report length
is incorrect, and large batches are much too slow. Repair both without changing APIs.
Only `app/window.py` and `app/report.py` are editable. `app/parser.py` is trusted,
working support code and must remain unchanged.

Each nonblank input line is `request_id|error_code`. Whitespace is stripped, blank
lines are ignored, and malformed records raise ValueError. Error codes are nonempty,
case-sensitive strings; repeated request IDs do not deduplicate records. K is an
integer >= 0. Negative K raises ValueError. Up to 200000 parsed records are assessed.

`longest_window(codes, k)` returns (start, end_exclusive) in the PARSED record array.
Choose the longest contiguous span with at most k distinct codes; if lengths tie,
choose the earliest start. No eligible span (including k=0) returns (0, 0).
`build_report(lines, k)` returns {"start": start, "end_exclusive": end, "length": end-start}.
Preserve parsing, tie-breaking and empty-input behavior. Do not mutate input.
Use an O(n) sliding window with hashing for code frequencies; do not repeatedly scan
or copy a growing window. An assessed 200000-record window call must finish in <2s;
the whole task has a 10-second wall-clock limit. Only standard-library code is allowed.

Example 1:
Input: lines=["r1|A", "r2|B", "r3|A", "r4|C", "r5|C"], k=2
Output: {"start": 0, "end_exclusive": 3, "length": 3}
The later span [A,C,C] ties in length, so the earlier span [A,B,A] wins.

Example 2:
Input: lines=["r1|A", "r2|B", "r3|C", "r4|C", "r5|B", "r6|B", "r7|A"], k=2
Output: {"start": 1, "end_exclusive": 6, "length": 5}
